distinguishing_features: Converts swelling-induced mechanical strain into a measurable electrical resistance change via an infused piezoresistive nanocomposite network, rather than inferring a degradation proxy from existing flow/pressure telemetry.
Embeds electrodes directly in the consumable blanket so the sensing element is co-located with the failure site, not a separate external transducer.
Electrically reads the precursor strain continuously in real time via the machine PLC, instead of inferring from an already-instrumented hydraulic variable.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Provide continuous, in-situ early detection of swell-induced degradation of a consumable blanket before it manifests as registration drift, without disassembly or manual periodic measurement.
parsed.viable_reason: Piezoresistive nanocomposite strain sensing into a resistance rise is physically plausible and the stated 5% swell to 10% signal vs 0.5% resolution is coherent and testable via the given protocol.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Integrating a piezoresistive nanocomposite gauge into the consumable blanket to transduce swelling strain directly is not a routine application of the closest pressure/telemetry proxy art and is not an obvious substitution.
